Mr. Nikhil Ajmera
For Respondent(s) : Mr. DS Nimla  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MADAN GOPAL VYAS
Judgment DATE OF JUDGMENT: 18/09/2023

The present civil misc. appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant-claimant against the judgment and award dated 3.2.2010 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajsamand (hereinafter referred to as the learned tribunal for short) in MAC Case No.69/2005, whereby the claim petition filed by the appellant-claimant was rejected.

2. The facts in brief are that the appellant-claimant preferred a claim petition before the learned tribunal seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.5,97,000/- for an accident which took place on 27.10.2004.

In the claim petition, it was stated that at 3.00 PM (2 of 5) [CMA-374/2010] on 27.10.2004 when the appellant-claimant alongwith his friend was going on his motorcycle number RJ-30-M-0185 from Baneriya to Rajayawas, then a truck bearing no.RJ-27-G-0953, which was being driven rashly and negligently by the driver, hit the motorcycle of the appellant-claimant,
resulting into fracture on his right leg and injuries to the pillion rider too.

It was further stated that for the said accident, an FIR bearing No.184/2004 was lodged at Police Station, Rajnagar and after investigation, the police filed challan against the driver of the truck for the offences under Sections 279 and 337 of the IPC.
Therefore, claiming the above compensation, the claim petition was filed.

sentences.text: Leaned counsel appearing for the appellant-claimant submits that the claim petition was rejected by the learned tribunal solely on the ground that in the FIR lodged, the truck number mentioned was RJ-30-1774, whereas in the investigation, the investigating agency found that the offending vehicle was truck bearing number RJ-27-G-0953.

Learned counsel submits that actually the offending vehicle was truck number RJ-27-G-0953 and not the truck number RJ-30-1774, which is very much clear not only from the claim petition whereby appellant-claimants have mentioned the offending vehicle's number as RJ-27-G-0953, but also from the challan filed by the investigating agency as well as from the mauka report (Ex.3) dated 28.10.2004 and from the notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act (Ex.6) sent to the driver of the offending vehicle, where too, the driver has admitted that the offending vehicle being truck number RJ-27-G-0953 was driven by him and the accident occurred on 27.10.2004 at 3.00 PM.

It is submitted that merely on the basis of the fact that in the FIR, the truck number was mentioned as RJ-30-1774 and the respondent-Insurance Company in its reply to the claim petition stated that the offending vehicle was truck number RJ-30-1774, the learned tribunal has rejected the claim petition in it entirety.

Learned counsel submits that the learned tribunal has not appreciated the evidence either oral or documentary in its right perspective and therefore, the present civil misc.
appeal deserves to be allowed.
5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent- insurance company opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the appellant.

Learned counsel for the respondent-insurance company submits that the impugned judgment has rightly been passed by the learned tribunal after considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and the same does not warrant any interference.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. On minute scrutiny of the entire record as well as perusal of the impugned judgment, it is amply clear that the learned tribunal committed grave illegality while passing the impugned judgment.

This Court finds that though in the FIR the truck number was mentioned as RJ-30-1774, but in the entire documentary evidence, i.e., in claim petition, or in the challan papers, or in the mauka report or even in the notice under Section 133 of the MV Act sent to the driver of the offending vehicle, the vehicle number shown is RJ-27-G-0953.

Not only this, even the driver has (4 of 5) [CMA-374/2010]
admitted in the receipt of notice under Section 133 of the MV Act that his truck collied with the motorcycle bearing Number RJ-30- M-0185, resulting into accident on 27.10.2004 at 3.00 pm.
Thus, apparently, it is clear that the learned tribunal has not considered the oral as well as the documentary evidence in its correct perspective and has rejected the claim petition in its entirety.

The Motor Vehicle Act is mainly concerned with granting relief to illeterate and innocent people on the road, who are frequent victims of accidents and then find themselves without a claim to the compensation that they should normally receive.

The Motor Vehicles Act is a social legislation,
therfore, strict rule of evidence is also not applicable.

In the present case, the aforesaid right has been denied to the appellant only on account of the fact that in the FIR, the truck number was Dhan Singh vs Gautam Lal And Ors on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59991633/
2 wrongly mentioned as RJ-30- 1774.

sentences.text: The learned tribunal, thus, failed to consider and evaluate the evidence available on record properly.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to remand the matter back to the learned tribunal to decide the same afresh.
8. In view of the above, this civil appeal is allowed.

The impugned judgment dated 3.2.2010 passed by the learned tribunal passed in MAC Case No.69/2005 is quashed and set aside and the matter is remanded back to the learned tribunal to decide the same afresh in accordance with law as early as possible preferably on or before 31.12.2023.
9.
All the parties are directed to appear before the learned tribunal on 10.10.2023.
Office is directed to send the record of the learned tribunal forthwith.
11. Office is further directed to send a copy of this order to the learned tribunal either by FAX or by email forthwith.

(MADAN GOPAL VYAS),J 113-CPGoyal/-
